setupSteps.title: Install Git
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Git responds with a version number

setupSteps.title: Install Node LTS
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Node responds with a version number

steps.title: Open Terminal
steps.body: Keep it open beside Iris.
steps.verifierLabel: Terminal is open

steps.title: Check Git and Node
steps.body: Use Terminal. Git and the current Node LTS are required.
steps.verifierLabel: Git and Node respond with version numbers

hints: No version for git? Run xcode-select --install and let Apple's installer finish.
Node missing? Install the LTS from nodejs.org, then open a fresh Terminal window.

steps.title: Install pnpm
steps.body: The interface is a pnpm project.
steps.verifierLabel: pnpm responds with a version number

expect.prompt: In the shell, has `npm install -g pnpm` finished — a summary line such as "added 1 package" or "changed 1 package", with the prompt back and no error? Answer not done while it is still downloading, or if it stopped on a permissions error such as EACCES.

hints: If npm reported a permissions error, install Node from nodejs.org rather than a system package manager.
Command finished but nothing found? Open a fresh Terminal window so the new PATH is picked up.

steps.title: Install Rust
steps.body: Already have cargo? This step is already done. Otherwise rustup.rs shows one command to paste.
steps.verifierLabel: cargo responds with a version number

expect.prompt: In the terminal, has the rustup installer finished — a line such as "Rust is installed now. Great!", with the prompt back and no error? Answer not done while it is still downloading or still asking which installation option to use.

hints: Already have Rust? This step is finished the moment cargo answers — nothing is reinstalled.
Already finished? Open a new Terminal window — cargo only joins the PATH of new shells.

steps.title: Copy Hickeyfield to this Mac
steps.command:
cd ~
if [ ! -d hickeyfield/.git ]; then
git clone https://github.com/Blueturboguy07/hickeyfield.git
fi
steps.verifierLabel: A hickeyfield folder appears

hints: If it stopped partway, delete the hickeyfield folder and run the command again.
Permission denied? Run it from your home folder rather than a synced or network drive.

steps.title: Open the hickeyfield folder
steps.verifierLabel: Your terminal prompt is inside the hickeyfield folder

steps.title: Use the reviewed version
steps.verifierLabel: Git reports the reviewed commit

steps.title: Install the interface packages
steps.verifierLabel: The install finishes without an error

steps.title: Fetch the video engine
steps.body: About 80 MB. The script checks its licence before installing it.
steps.verifierLabel: It reports GPL, not nonfree, and finishes

hints: Permission denied? Run bash scripts/fetch-ffmpeg.sh instead.
Stopped partway? Run it again; it keeps what it already downloaded.

steps.title: Build the app
steps.body: The first build compiles the whole Rust core, so give it a while.
steps.verifierLabel: A Hickeyfield.app appears in the bundle folder

steps.title: Put Hickeyfield in Applications
steps.body: Copy the freshly built app into Applications so it's a real, launchable Mac app.
steps.verifierLabel: Hickeyfield.app is in your Applications folder

steps.title: Open Hickeyfield
steps.body: Built on your own machine, so macOS opens it without any warning.
steps.verifierLabel: Hickeyfield opens

steps.title: Get a fal key
steps.body: Sign in, make a key, and copy it. You pay fal directly for what you generate.
steps.verifierLabel: You have a key on your clipboard

hints: The key is shown once. Copy it before closing the dialog.
Already have one saved? Use it — there is no need to make another.

steps.title: Paste the key into Hickeyfield
steps.body: Settings, then fal, then Test. It is stored in your keychain, never in a file.
steps.verifierLabel: Hickeyfield reports the key works

hints: Nothing happened? Press Test beside the field rather than Enter.
Set the key from a terminal instead? Remove it and paste it in the app — a key installed by another program cannot be read back by this one.

steps.title: Make something
steps.body: Type a shot, check the price on the button, and press Generate.
steps.verifierLabel: A video appears in the middle column and plays

Command finished but nothing found? Open a fresh PowerShell window so the new PATH is picked up.

steps.title: Install the C++ build tools
steps.body: Tick Desktop development with C++, then install. Rust uses Microsoft's linker.
steps.verifierLabel: The installer reports it finished

point.descriptor: the Desktop development with C++ workload tile

steps.title: Install Rust
steps.body: Download rustup-init.exe, run it, then reopen PowerShell.
steps.verifierLabel: cargo responds with a version number

expect.prompt: In the shell, has the rustup installer finished — a line such as "Rust is installed now. Great!", with the prompt back and no error? Answer not done while it is still downloading or still asking which installation option to use.

hints: Run the downloaded rustup-init.exe and take the default install.
Already finished? Close PowerShell and open a new window so cargo is on the PATH.

steps.title: Install CMake
steps.body: Pick the Windows x64 installer and let it add CMake to PATH.
steps.verifierLabel: cmake responds with a version number

point.descriptor: the Windows x64 Installer row ending in .msi

steps.title: Install NASM
steps.body: The assembler the encryption library needs. Take the win64 installer.
steps.verifierLabel: NASM is installed and on your PATH

point.descriptor: the newest version folder, then win64, then the installer ending in .exe
